<description>
`ConsumeNodeSmart` draws `older()/after()` values from `[1, 0x7FFFFFF]`, one F short of the `[1, 0x7FFFFFFF] `range used by the stable target. `after()` never reaches `LOCKTIME_THRESHOLD`, so `miniscript_smart` never builds time-based `after()` nodes and never exercises the height/time timelock mixing checks in `ComputeType`.

Use `std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max()` for the bound in both targets instead of hand-counted hex literals.

With the fix, replaying the existing qa-assets corpus hits the mixing branches that previously had 0 hits (libFuzzer edges go from 8829 to 8841), and a 5 minute run covers the remaining ones. The corpus stays valid since the byte consumption stays the same.
</description>
